question_text: Lauren deposits $\$10\,000$ in an account that compounds interest monthly. $4.5$ years later, the account has balance $\$12\,000$.

subparts.stem: What annual rate of interest did the account pay?
subparts.solution:
$$N = 4.5 \times 12 = 54, \quad PV = -10\,000, \quad PMT = 0, \quad FV = 12\,000, \quad P/Y = 12, \quad C/Y = 12$$
$$\therefore I\% \approx 4.06$$
$$\text{The account paid about } 4.06\% \text{ interest per annum.}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: Use the GDC TVM Solver to calculate the annual nominal interest rate $I\%$ from compound interest parameters.
step_by_step: Input known values: $PV = -10000$ (cash outflow), $FV = 12000$ (cash inflow), $P/Y = C/Y = 12$.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Giving both $PV$ and $FV$ the same sign in the financial calculator, which results in an error.

subparts.stem: How long will it take Lauren to double her deposit?

mark_breakdown.desc: Setting up TVM parameters with doubled investment: $FV = 20000$, $PV = -10000$, $I\% = 4.06$
Rounding up to next whole compounding period: 206 months or 17 years and 2 months

subparts.solution:
$$I\% = 4.06, \quad PV = -10\,000, \quad PMT = 0, \quad FV = 20\,000, \quad P/Y = 12, \quad C/Y = 12$$
$$\therefore N \approx 205.2$$
$$\text{It will take } 206 \text{ months or } 17 \text{ years and } 2 \text{ months for Lauren to double her deposit.}$$

ai_explanation.concept_rule: When compounding occurs at discrete intervals, the number of compounding periods must be rounded up to ensure the target is reached.
step_by_step: Since interest is credited monthly, round up to $206$ full months.
Convert months to years: $206 = 17 \times 12 + 2$, giving 17 years and 2 months.
ai_explanation.common_pitfalls: Rounding down to 205 months, at which point the deposit has not yet doubled.
